podcast.title: Signing of Death Grips (2012)
podcast.body: Epic Records signed Death Grips in early 2012 for a contract spanning two or three albums, having been impressed by the rapid circulation and popularity of their "Ex-Military" mixtape. This signing marked the beginning of a "very complicated relationship" between the band and the label. "en cuanto la caza Epic Records a los pocos meses en el primeros del 2012, Fitch a los Dead Gryps por dos tres discos, una relación que sería muy complicada."

podcast.title: Signed Bobby Shmurda (2014)
podcast.body: Epic Records signed Jamaican-American rapper Akeel Pollard, known as Bobby Shmurda, in 2014. This signing occurred during the two months when his Vine clip featuring the "Shmoney Dance" gained over three million views, demonstrating the influence of viral social media activity on major label decisions. "Shmerda signed with epic records."

podcast.title: Audioslave Co-Release (First Album) – Partnership with Interscope
podcast.body: For Audioslave's debut album, Epic Records, which was Rage Against the Machine's label, collaborated with Interscope Records (Chris Cornell's label) for a joint release. This arrangement was part of a complex compromise to accommodate both artists' existing contracts. "The first album would be released by both Epic, Rage Against the Machine's label, and Interscope, Chris's label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Audioslave Release (Third Album for Rest of World) – Continued Involvement
podcast.body: Epic Records continued its involvement with Audioslave for their third album, handling its release for the rest of the world, while Interscope managed the US release. This demonstrated an ongoing, albeit split, relationship with the supergroup. "then the third album would be Interscope for the US and Epic for the rest of the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Conflict over "No Love Deep Web" Release and Censorship
podcast.body: Epic Records faced further problems with Death Grips regarding the release of "No Love Deep Web," which was delayed for months due to the label's issues with its controversial and censored cover art. "Esto generaría más problemas todavía de Dead Gryps con Epic Records y al final el lanzamiento de No Love de Web quedaría redrasado durante meses por enormes problemas censurados con su portada."

podcast.title: Dismissal of Death Grips from Label
podcast.body: After Death Grips defiantly released portions of their unapproved third album for free, Epic Records became "very angry" with them and ultimately expelled the band from the label. "Epic Records acaba muy cabreada con ellos y los acaba expulsando de la disco gráfica."

podcast.title: Dispute over "The Money Store" Release
podcast.body: A major dispute arose when Death Grips released their album "The Money Store" for free online before its scheduled market release, causing significant friction with Epic Records. "tendrían una gran disputa por Epic Records porque ellos la publicarían de manera gratuita antes de salir al mercado como disco."

podcast.title: Leaked Emails and Monetization Efforts
podcast.body: Following their dismissal, Death Grips published private emails between the band and Epic Records. These emails exposed the complicated relationship and revealed "somewhat murky" attempts by Epic Records to further monetize Death Grips' music. "se veía esa complicada relación y asuntos son tanto turbios de Epic Records de cómo intentaba monetizar más todavía la música de Dead Gryps."

podcast.title: Pearl Jam Signing
podcast.body: Pearl Jam signed with Epic Records, a major label, after initially performing under the name Mookie Blaylock, marking a significant step in their career. "by the time the band signed to epic records Mookie Blaylock had changed their name to Pearl Jam."

podcast.title: Rage Against The Machine Contract
podcast.body: Epic Records successfully signed Rage Against The Machine following a bidding war among major labels. The agreement was secured because Epic acceded to all of the band's demands, including maintaining full creative control, recognizing that their extensive worldwide distribution and marketing power were crucial for the band to convey its political message effectively. "Epic was the major that agreed to all of Rage's demands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rage Against The Machine Live Album
podcast.body: Epic Records released Rage Against The Machine's live album from the Democratic National Convention 2001. "le pende directo por Epic Records, el democrático nacional convention 2001."

podcast.title: Refusal to Allow Rapid Album Release
podcast.body: Epic Records refused to permit Death Grips to release a third album within a year, stating that releasing three albums in such a short period was "a bit of an abuse." This refusal led to further escalation of tensions. "Epic Records se niega porque dice que sacar tres albumes en un año que ya empieza a ser un poco un abuso."

podcast.title: Threat of Lawsuit
podcast.body: The publication of the private emails on Facebook almost led to a substantial lawsuit from Epic Records against Death Grips, though the legal action ultimately did not materialize. "Casi les vale una demanda bastante importante de Epic Records por la publicación de todos estos correos electrónicos en Facebook pero al final se queda en nada."
